title: Annual Ghost Walk returns to Sweetwater County Library
excerpt: GREEN RIVER -- Those curious about what happens after dark at the Sweetwater County Library will have two opportunities this October to find out for themselves.
content:
GREEN RIVER -- Those curious about what happens after dark at the Sweetwater County Library will have two opportunities this October to find out for themselves.

The Ghost Walk Crew, a part of the Sweetwater County Library Foundation, will host public paranormal investigations at the Sweetwater County Library in Green River on Saturday, Oct. 10 and Saturday, Oct. 24, with investigations beginning at 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. each night.

Tickets are $20 per person, with a maximum of two tickets per person. Each investigation is limited to just 20 participants, allowing for a smaller, more personalized experience. Space is limited, and advance ticket purchases are encouraged as they sell out quickly. The 9 p.m. investigations are already almost sold out.

Tickets can be purchased online at https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/ghost-walk-crew-halloween-investigation

Unlike a traditional ghost tour, the events give participants an opportunity to take part in an actual paranormal investigation inside the library. Guests will join the Ghost Walk Crew as they explore the building after hours, learn about its history and reported paranormal activity, and use paranormal investigation equipment in an attempt to collect evidence of their own.

“A haunted library is the only place where a shush from the dark actually makes your hair stand up. And boy, do we get shushed!” Tiffany Kennah, Ghost Walk Crew member, said.

The Sweetwater County Library has developed a reputation over the years for unexplained activity, making it an ideal setting for those interested in local history, the paranormal or simply looking for a unique October experience.

“We’re excited to bring back this long-standing community tradition and give residents another opportunity to experience the library in a completely different way,” said Lisa Frint, Executive Director of the Sweetwater County Library Foundation. “The Ghost Walk has always been a popular event, especially for those who have an interest in the paranormal, and it offers a unique, hands-on experience right here in our community. We’re also working to expand the Ghost Walk Crew’s event lineup and create some new experiences, so we encourage everyone to stay tuned as there’s more to come.”

Proceeds from the Ghost Walk investigations benefit the Sweetwater County Library Foundation and its efforts to support the libraries and the Community Fine Arts Center throughout Sweetwater County.

The October investigations are part of the Ghost Walk Crew’s broader effort to share local history and lore, introduce the public to paranormal investigation techniques and equipment, and raise funds to support the Library Foundation’s mission. There is also a new Facebook page for the Ghost Walk Crew which can be found at www.Facebook.com/GhostWalkCrew. Residents are encouraged to follow the page for the latest updates and event happenings.
